patch_description:
This candidate merges the two strongest parent designs. From the "theta" seed (score 0.80, convergence in 60 steps) it keeps the extreme parameter-economy trick of driving *all three* rotation axes (RX, RY, RZ) with a single shared scalar parameter `theta` per block repetition — this pre/post-entanglement multi-axis rotation with one parameter was empirically the fastest-converging design. From the `p_shared` ring+skip-2 seed it borrows the richer, still completely parameter-free, entangling topology.

The entangling layer is upgraded to a union of three fixed, non-parametric CZ patterns forming a small expander graph on the 8-qubit ring:
  - distance-1 edges (nearest-neighbor ring, from both parents),
  - distance-2 "skip" edges (from the `p_shared` seed), and
  - distance-4 "diameter" edges (from the `theta` seed).

Together every qubit gets degree-3 (or 4) fixed entangling connectivity, maximizing expressivity/generalization at zero extra parameter cost, while the single shared `theta` scalar keeps the trainable-parameter count as small as the best-performing prior candidates (1 unique name per block, matching the fastest-converging seed). This aims to combine the "fast convergence" property of the RX+RY+RZ single-parameter idea with the "denser fixed entanglement" property of the ring+skip topology, hopefully improving robustness/generalization while preserving parameter economy and convergence speed.
